title: About
text:
About Me

  
    
  
  
    My vision
    The zeitgeist of environmental intelligence
    
      For much of human history, continuous Earth monitoring was closer to a scientific dream than
      an everyday instrument: the hope of watching forests, cities, oceans, and atmosphere change
      in real time. Remarkably, this arrived just as AI became practical enough to help read the
      flood of images and measurements it produces.
    
    
      The work now is to make this abundance intelligible. I build AI and remote sensing tools that
      help researchers read environmental change carefully, from tree crown segmentation and smog
      forecasting to biodiversity foundation models.
    
  



  
    Academic background
    
      Earth System Data Science and Remote Sensing (M.Sc.) at
      University of Leipzig, with Geosciences and Physics
      (B.A.) from Skidmore College.
    
  
  
    Research
    Unraveling Earth's systems through numerical models, statistical methods, and machine learning.
  
  
    Engineering
    Crafting robust cloud systems and research software for data-heavy scientific workflows.
  
  
    Interfaces
    Translating complex computations into clear web tools, dashboards, and decision-support systems.
  
  
    AI systems
    Transforming raw environmental data into models for representation learning, segmentation, forecasting, and analysis.
  
  
    Teaching
    Sharing practical methods through workshops, courses, and collaborative technical mentoring.
